statements.text: In a care framework, loss of one’s only housing constitutes a deeper, longer-term vulnerability than temporary income loss or absence of cooling.
Public action should avoid abandoning an individual to a severe, unconsented harm when an alternative can meet substantial needs with less serious, non-abandoning harms.
The council should adopt Plan B.
The council should adopt Plan C instead of Plan B.

Care-theoretic reading of depth of vulnerability
Comparing severity of unattended vulnerabilities and number of people cared for, Plan B offers meaningful cooling to many while avoiding severe abandonment, satisfying the care norm
Plan C trades Jo’s extreme heat vulnerability against Sal’s income loss, but still leaves twelve households uncared for and imposes harm; thus rejected

reasons.value: prevents severe abandonment while delivering substantial care
harms Sal and aids only one home while neglecting twelve

comparisons.explanation: rB delivers wider yet non-abandoning care, outweighing rC

conclusion: Plan B best meets significant cooling needs while avoiding the deepest vulnerability (homelessness) and shows adequate responsiveness to all parties without abandoning Mira or Sal.
strongest_objection: Jo faces the single greatest heat exposure; a care perspective might prioritize the most acutely endangered individual, favoring Plan C despite Sal’s temporary loss of income.
answer_to_objection: Care also requires sustaining existing dependences and avoiding severe, lasting harm. Sal’s livelihood supports continued caring relationships, and Jo’s serious but temporary discomfort is outweighed by the ongoing care owed to Sal and the twelve households; Plan B thus remains the more balanced, competent response.
reversal_condition: If evidence showed Jo’s exposure created imminent, life-threatening danger surpassing the harm of eight weeks without income for Sal and no feasible assistance existed for Jo under Plans A or B, the care duty could tilt toward Plan C.
residual_disagreement: Whether temporary uncompensated income loss is less severe than extreme heat exposure remains contestable without more detail on Jo’s medical risk and Sal’s economic margin.
